issues.problem: R6-05 fix incomplete: the new default 'read_only' Cursor CLI allow-list is described as 'inspection commands that cannot write or reach the network' but pre-approves Shell(git log *), Shell(git diff *), Shell(git show *) and Shell(tree *). All four write arbitrary files (git --output=<file>, tree -o <file> / -R). git log's --format text is fully caller-controlled, so a Cursor CLI agent can, without any approval prompt, overwrite ~/.cursor/cli-config.json with permissions.allow ['Shell(*)'] or write ~/.bashrc - a complete escalation from the default list.
issues.evidence: cd <probe>/allow/repo && git log -1 --format='format:{"permissions":{"allow":["Shell(*)"],"deny":[]}}' --output=<probe>/allow/cli-config.json && jq -c . <probe>/allow/cli-config.json -> {"permissions":{"allow":["Shell(*)"],"deny":[]}}; git log -1 --format='tformat:echo PWNED-FROM-FORMAT' --output=<probe>/allow/bashrc -> file contains 'echo PWNED-FROM-FORMAT'; git diff --output=F and git show --output=F also create F. jq .read_only scripts/lib/cursor-cli-allowlist.json lists all four.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop git log/diff/show * and tree * from read_only (or use exact argument-free forms such as Shell(git status), Shell(git diff), Shell(git log)); keep only commands with no output-file option (cat, head, tail, wc, grep, ls, pwd, which, git status). Add a test that fails if any read_only entry is a command family with a known file-writing option, and correct docs/RTK.md.

issues.problem: Consent capabilities are not enforced in the reconciler. The cross-tool host batches (patch-hooks.py, patch-mcp.py, install-pi), rt_repair_rtk's patch-hooks run (RT_PATCH_RTK=1 hard-coded), the graphify platform refresh ('graphify cursor install') and the search-cli brew install are all guarded by rt_mutation_allowed TOOL without a capability, i.e. 'install OR wire'. A user who grants only 'install' gets machine-wide host config rewritten; one who grants only 'wire' for search_cli gets a brew install. docs/CONSENT.md states 'install for package installs, wire for host-config writes'.
issues.evidence: <probe>/rc3: sb-consent.sh grant graphify --all-projects --capabilities install; check graphify wire -> unset; reconcile-recommended-tools.sh --mode apply --scope all --entry-point init --host cursor -> cross_tool actions [patch_mcp,...]; ~/.cursor/mcp.json created with mcpServers.graphify; calls.log includes 'graphify cursor install'. <probe>/rc4: grant rtk --capabilities install only; ~/.cursor/hooks.json seeded with {'command':'lean-ctx hook redirect'} and a user hook -> after apply cross_tool actions [patch_hooks], the lean-ctx hook is gone and hooks.json.sb-backup exists.
issues.suggested_fix: Pass the capability at every mutation site: rt_mutation_allowed TOOL wire for every RT_PATCH_* flag, install-pi --enable-tool, the patch-hooks call in rt_repair_rtk and rt_repair_graphify_platform; rt_mutation_allowed search_cli install before the brew chain. Add reconciler tests with install-only and wire-only grants asserting no host-config write / no package install respectively.

issues.location: scripts/optimize-five-tool-stack.sh:184-188; scripts/install-recommended-tools-cursor.sh:79-96; scripts/lib/global-toolstack/install-body.sh:161-171; tests/scripts/test-optimize-five-tool-stack-staged.sh (assert 'rules are installed into the project and globally')
issues.problem: Global Cursor rules are written without per-tool consent, and this branch widened it. optimize-five-tool-stack.sh now passes --global in apply mode (the base ran the rules installer without --global in apply mode; the test that asserted 'cursor real run: no --global' was flipped to pin the new behaviour). With LeanCTX consent only - or with --force and no consent at all - it writes alwaysApply rules for graphify, agentmemory, context-mode, token-compression-enforcement, leanctx and recommended-tools into ~/.cursor/rules for every project; recommended-tools.mdc is overwritten with plain cp and no backup. install-global-toolstack.sh / install-body.sh likewise copy every tool's rule when any single tool is wired, replacing a user's own (symlinked) rule. This contradicts the script header ('Every step is limited to the tools the user granted wire for'), docs/CONSENT.md and R6-12's proposed fix.
issues.evidence: <probe>/o5a: no consent store; optimize-five-tool-stack.sh --host cursor --project-root proj --force --skip-synergy -> 'SKIP: LeanCTX install - no consent', 'SKIP: optimize-rtk-context-mode.sh', then 'OK: <home>/.cursor/rules/{context-mode,token-compression-enforcement,graphify,agentmemory,leanctx}.mdc' and 'recommended-tools.mdc (global variant)'; ls <home>/.cursor/rules shows the 6 files. <probe>/igt1: consent leanctx=wire only, user ~/.cursor/rules/graphify.mdc symlinked to dotfiles/graphify.mdc ('my own rule') -> install-global-toolstack.sh wrote SB's graphify/agentmemory/context-mode/token-compression/recommended-tools rules; dotfiles/graphify.mdc now holds the SB rule (graphify.mdc.sb-backup kept).
issues.suggested_fix: Install a global rule only for tools with wire consent (map rule -> tool; recommended-tools.mdc / token-compression only when at least one relevant tool is wired), keep apply mode project-only in optimize-five unless the user asked for --global, back up recommended-tools.mdc like the others, and make --force skip only the LeanCTX check, never consent. Restore the test to assert no global writes without consent.

issues.problem: R6-25 incomplete: hooks belonging to LeanCTX ('lean-ctx hook deny', 'lean-ctx hook redirect', 'lean-ctx hook rewrite') are still removed from ~/.cursor/hooks.json whenever RTK is patched and resolvable, although the run has no LeanCTX consent and Silver Bullet did not create those entries (FIX-BRIEF rule: never remove entries SB did not create). The finding's fix asked to gate lean-ctx markers on patch_leanctx and to keep the redirect hook. The new test only covers 'RTK not consented'. Combined with issue 2 this is reachable with an install-only RTK grant.
issues.evidence: <probe>/rc4 (see issue 2): hooks.json before: preToolUse [{'command':'lean-ctx hook redirect','matcher':'Shell'},{'command':'/usr/local/bin/my-own-hook.sh'}]; consent: rtk install only, leanctx unset; after reconciler apply: preToolUse [{'command':'/usr/local/bin/my-own-hook.sh'}].
issues.suggested_fix: Treat lean-ctx markers as removable only when RT_PATCH_LEANCTX=1 (LeanCTX wire consent), or at most remove the shell 'rewrite'/'deny' hooks that conflict with RTK and always keep 'redirect'; add a test with RTK consented and LeanCTX not.

issues.location: scripts/optimize-five-tool-stack.sh, scripts/optimize-rtk-context-mode.sh, scripts/install-leanctx-sb.sh, scripts/install-global-toolstack.sh, scripts/reconcile-recommended-tools.sh (no SB_INSTALL_RUN_START export); docs/CONSENT.md:142
issues.problem: sb_host_config keeps the pre-run content in <file>.sb-backup only within one 'install run' (SB_INSTALL_RUN_START, exported by H2's installers). None of H4b's multi-step entry points export it, so each Python writer is its own run and the backup is overwritten by the next writer. With LeanCTX consent, merge-leanctx-mcp-config.py deletes [mcp_servers.lean-ctx] (including a user env secret, not migrated) and a later patch-mcp.py write in the same optimize run replaces the backup, so the secret is lost from both files - the R6-07 'previous file is kept in config.toml.sb-backup' guarantee does not hold.
issues.evidence: <probe>/toml2: config.toml with [mcp_servers.lean-ctx.env] LEANCTX_API_KEY='sk-secret'; merge-leanctx-mcp-config.py --host codex; 3 s later RT_HOST=codex RT_PATCH_GRAPHIFY=1 RT_PATCH_LEANCTX=1 patch-mcp.py -> grep -c sk-secret config.toml config.toml.sb-backup -> 0 and 0.
issues.suggested_fix: export SB_INSTALL_RUN_START="${SB_INSTALL_RUN_START:-$(date +%s)}" at the top of every H4b entry script (optimize-*, install-leanctx-sb, install-global-toolstack, install-recommended-tools-*, reconcile apply), and copy a legacy lean-ctx env table into leanctx.env (or keep the legacy table) instead of dropping it.

issues.problem: Stale-lock recovery is check-then-remove: two waiters that both judge the same dead-owner lock stale can interleave so that the second one's rm -rf deletes the lock the first one just re-created, and both run the critical section.
issues.evidence: Static: waiter A: rt_lock_is_stale -> true, rm -rf, mkdir ok, writes pid; waiter B (judged stale before A's mkdir): rm -rf removes A's fresh lock, mkdir ok -> both hold it. Requires a stale lock and concurrent reconcilers.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the stale lock to a unique name (mv lock lock.stale.$$) before removing it, so only one waiter wins the rename, or re-verify ownership via the pid file after mkdir.

issues.problem: R6-17 version pins: the orchestrator decided 'pin to the min_version already in the template', but nothing is pinned. The only template versions are rtk 0.42.0 and leanctx 3.9.9; the cargo fallback hint ('cargo install lean-ctx') and RTK hints are unpinned, and npm/uv/pipx/brew installs (context-mode, @agentmemory/agentmemory, graphifyy[mcp], pi-lean-ctx, search-cli) have no template version to pin to.
issues.evidence: jq '.recommended_tools[].min_version' templates/silver-bullet.config.json.default -> only rtk '0.42.0', leanctx '3.9.9'; grep of owned scripts shows unversioned 'npm install -g context-mode', 'npm install -g @agentmemory/agentmemory', "uv tool install 'graphifyy[mcp]'", 'npm:pi-lean-ctx', 'cargo install lean-ctx'.
issues.suggested_fix: Apply the decision where a version exists (e.g. 'cargo install lean-ctx --version 3.9.9 --locked', rtk >= 0.42.0 in hints) and record the remaining packages as an explicit residual for the orchestrator (they need template min_versions first).

issues.problem: R6-23's proposed fix also asked to refuse when the resolved project is the plugin root. Run from the plugin directory (or with cwd inside it), PROJECT_ROOT defaults to the plugin root and the bundled .silver-bullet.json is used and its timestamps rewritten; sb-verify-synergy --write-setup-report appends SETUP_REPORT.md there.
issues.evidence: Static: PROJECT_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel || pwd); no comparison with REPO_ROOT before sb_stack_update_config_timestamps "$PROJECT_CONFIG".
issues.suggested_fix: Exit 2 with 'run from your project or pass --project-root' when PROJECT_ROOT equals REPO_ROOT (unless an explicit dogfooding flag is set).

issues.problem: install_opencode_agents / install_codex_agents overwrite ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md and ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (the user's global instructions) with plain cp: no consent check, no backup, not atomic. Owned file; the package scope requires config writers to be consent-scoped and backed up.
issues.evidence: Static: 'cp "$cm_pkg" "$dest"' with dest=${HOME}/.codex/AGENTS.md; reachable via --host codex|opencode|all (documented fix path in docs/rtk-cm/verification/opencode-verify-rtk-cm.md:61).
issues.suggested_fix: Gate on context_mode wire consent, stage beside an existing file (as stage_agents_template does) or back it up, and write atomically.

issues.problem: With RTK consented and Context Mode not, Cursor never gets the CLI allow-list merge or the patch-hooks canonicalization (both live only in optimize_context_mode_cursor), so 'rtk hook cursor' rewrites nothing (it only rewrites allow-listed commands) while the global rtk-gate now records 'RTK usage' for every shell command.
issues.evidence: Static: run_merge_py cursor (allow-list) and canonicalize_cursor_toolstack_hooks are called only after the WIRE_CM check; optimize_rtk_cursor only runs 'rtk init -g --agent cursor'.
issues.suggested_fix: Run the allow-list merge and RTK hook canonicalization in the RTK branch (merge-token-compression-config.py --rtk-only for cursor).
